descriptions.text: Gnomish Drop Bear. Contraption. This is one of the Dirigible Gnome's earliest fast-attack planes. There are only a handful of these still in service. While able to quickly reach most targets when drop-launched from home base, the twin engines of these early models were famously underpowered. Damaged Drop Bears oftentimes had difficulty obtaining enough altitude to reach home, even after ditching their payload. This is why most of these planes carry rapid-deploying, quick-escape balloons, making them sitting targets for enemy aircraft and flak. … Don't worry, these guys don't drop bombs. Their standard payload is something much more entertaining.

beats.headline: A buzzsaw overhead
beats.text: A plane rockets by a hundred feet over their heads, whining like a flying buzzsaw. It must have dropped from the Wasteland: an open-air biplane, an engine nestled between the wings on each side, a red-hatted gnome pilot and a second gnome facing backward. A screaming grey animal like a jacked-up rabid koala is painted on its nose, and two egg-shaped objects hang under it in small nets. Carl's smoke curtains do not hide them. As it lines up thirty feet off the ground, Donut teleports them away, and the object it drops where they stood clangs, bounces once, and does nothing.

beats.headline: Smoke from one engine
beats.text: Carl's full-strength hob-lobber goes off in mid-air, much too low and behind the fast plane, but the biplane shudders and smoke trails from one of its two engines. It banks away and climbs, fleeing the fight. The metallic egg it dropped is the size of a garbage can, and nothing moves. Katia, watching the plane, sees it turning into a balloon; it has dropped the second bomb way over there, and that did not go off either. Their engine went out, says Carl; they are deploying their escape balloon.

beats.headline: Death Trap, renamed
beats.text: Louis, Firas and Langley have secured an intact Drop Bear, its pilot nowhere to be found, and covered it with a tarp at the edge of the other town. It runs on actual gasoline, and Carl fills the tank only a quarter of the way to keep it light; there are no bombs left under the wings. It looks like something a drunk built in his backyard out of scrap metal. Wiping the dust off the nose shows the rabid koala and, stencilled in Syndicate standard, the plane's name: Death Trap, with four bombs painted after it. Carl sprays over it and writes Nightmare II on the side.
